mainTopic: Who disqualifies a woman from כהונה, the אלמנת עיסה, doubtful versus definite flawed lineage (שתוקי), and whether a כותי may marry a כותית
overview: The amud opens with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's test: if a כהן may marry a man's daughter, he may also marry that man's widow. The גמרא shows that the תנא קמא, רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל all learn from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה, but each picks a different feature of that case. That is why they disagree about a מצרי שני and about a male convert from עמון or מואב. רב חסדא then rules that all three agree an אלמנת עיסה is unfit for כהונה. This goes against רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who allow her because of ספק ספיקא. Next, רב rules like רבי אליעזר that people whose flaw is doubtful may not marry those whose flaw is definite, and שמואל objects from הלל's version. This leads to a contradiction about the child of a pregnant ארוסה. The גמרא solves it either by switching the opinions or by reading the word שתוקי in several new ways. The amud ends with רבי אלעזר's ruling that a כותי may not marry a כותית. אביי rejects רב יוסף's reason for it, and רב דימי begins a new reason based on רבי ישמעאל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If you may marry his daughter, you may marry his widow
steps.stepSummary: The closing rule of the ברייתא links a man's daughter and his widow: a כהן may marry both, or neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone whose daughter you (a כהן) may marry, you may also marry his widow. Anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow either.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the teaching under discussion: the opinion of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which the גמרא quotes again in step 7. It gives a simple test for when a man's relationship with a woman disqualifies her from marrying a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test compares the man's daughter to his widow. If his daughter is fit for כהונה, then being with him did not damage the woman's status, so his widow is also fit. If his daughter is unfit, his widow is unfit too.

steps.title: What is the difference between the first opinion and רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case separates the תנא קמא from רבי יוסי in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between the first תנא and רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to sharpen the two opinions in the ברייתא. It wants a real case where they would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions seem to give the same results in the cases the ברייתא lists. The גמרא assumes they must differ somewhere, so it looks for the case where they split. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: they differ about a second-generation Egyptian
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the difference is a מצרי שני, and that both opinions learn from the case of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the difference between them is a second-generation Egyptian convert. Both of them learned their view only from the case of a כהן גדול with a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן names the case where the two opinions split: a מצרי שני who was with a Jewish woman. He also says both opinions come from the same source, which sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצרי שני may not marry into the Jewish people, but his children, the third generation, may. The question is whether being with him disqualifies a woman from marrying a כהן. Both sides compare this to כהן גדול באלמנה, but they draw different features from that model, and the גמרא explains each one next.

steps.title: The first opinion: any forbidden relationship disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא compares to כהן גדול באלמנה because that relationship is a sin, so any forbidden relationship disqualifies the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds: it is like a כהן גדול with a widow. Just as a כהן גדול with a widow is a forbidden relationship and disqualifies her, so too anyone whose relationship with her is forbidden disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the תנא קמא learns from כהן גדול באלמנה. The key feature he picks out is that the relationship itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the model case, the relationship is a sin and it disqualifies the woman. So the תנא קמא makes the rule: any forbidden relationship disqualifies. A מצרי שני is forbidden to her, so according to this view he disqualifies her.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only a man whose children are unfit disqualifies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי compares to כהן גדול באלמנה because the children are unfit, so only a man whose children are unfit disqualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds: it is like a כהן גדול with a widow. Just as a כהן גדול with a widow has children who are unfit, and he disqualifies her, so too anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוסי learns from the same case. He picks out a different feature: the children born from it are unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children of a כהן גדול with an אלמנה are חללים, unfit for כהונה. רבי יוסי makes this the key feature, so a man disqualifies the woman only if his children would be unfit. The forbidden nature of the relationship is not enough by itself.

steps.title: Why a second-generation Egyptian does not disqualify for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי's rule leaves out a מצרי שני, because a פסוק shows his descendants are not permanently unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This leaves out a second-generation Egyptian, whose children are not unfit, as the פסוק says: 'Children of the third generation who are born to them may enter the congregation of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רבי יוסי's rule to the מצרי שני and brings a פסוק to show that his children are not unfit. This finishes explaining where the two opinions split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the third generation may enter the קהל, so the line of a מצרי is not permanently flawed. Under רבי יוסי's rule he does not disqualify the woman. Under the תנא קמא's rule he does, because the relationship is still forbidden.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how two תנאים can learn from the very same source and still reach different results, depending on which feature of the model case they treat as the essential one.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: Daughter and widow go together
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a third opinion: if you may marry a man's daughter, you may marry his widow; if not, not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow. Anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the third opinion in the teaching, after the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a simple test: look at the man's daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is still which men make a woman unfit to marry a כהן when they have relations with her. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל ties the widow's status to the daughter's status. If a כהן could marry this man's daughter, he can also marry this man's widow.

steps.title: How is this different from רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is different from רבי יוסי, since they sound the same. This sets up עולא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said a man disqualifies her if his children are unfit. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it depends on whether his daughter is unfit. These seem to be the same rule, so the גמרא wants a case where they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What difference is there between Rabbi Yosei

steps.title: עולא: The difference is an Ammonite or Moabite convert
steps.stepSummary: עולא says they disagree about a male גר עמוני or מואבי, and both learn their rule from a כהן גדול with an אלמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The difference between them is a male Ammonite or Moabite convert. Both of them learned their rule only from a כהן גדול with a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question. The case where they disagree is a male convert from עמון or מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא also says both תנאים start from the same source, a כהן גדול with an אלמנה. They simply read that source differently. The next two steps explain each reading.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's reading: His children are unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reasons that a כהן גדול with an אלמנה disqualifies her because his children are unfit, so any man whose children are unfit disqualifies her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי holds it is like a כהן גדול with a widow. Just as a כהן גדול with a widow has unfit children and disqualifies her, so anyone whose children are unfit disqualifies her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוסי learns from the כהן גדול. The key feature, for him, is that the children come out unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A male עמוני's sons may not marry into the Jewish people. So for רבי יוסי his children count as unfit, and he disqualifies the woman from marrying a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: His children are unfit

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: כִּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּאַלְמָנָה

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reading: All his children, even daughters
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reasons that all of a כהן גדול's children from an אלמנה are unfit, even the daughters. That leaves out the עמוני and מואבי, whose daughters are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds it is like a כהן גדול with a widow. Just as a כהן גדול with a widow has all his children unfit, so too anyone whose children are all unfit, even the daughters. This leaves out the Ammonite and Moabite convert, whose daughters may enter the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from the same case. The key feature, for him, is that all the children are unfit, daughters too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daughters of an עמוני or מואבי are allowed to marry into the Jewish people, so not all of his children are unfit. That is why, for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, he does not disqualify the woman. This fits his rule of looking at the daughter.

steps.title: Proof that עמוני and מואבי daughters are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the claim that the daughters are allowed with a known teaching: 'an Ammonite man, not an Ammonite woman.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: An Ammonite man is forbidden, but not an Ammonite woman; a Moabite man, but not a Moabite woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the fact used in step 11, that women from עמון and מואב may marry into the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on marrying into the Jewish people applies only to the men of עמון and מואב. That is why the daughters of such a convert are fine. So for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, not all his children are unfit.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Everyone agrees about אלמנת עיסה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that all the תנאים agree a widow from a family of doubtful lineage is unfit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: All agree that a widow of questionable lineage is unfit for the priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רב חסדא says there is one case where all three opinions agree. The widow of a man from a family of doubtful lineage may not marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the תנאים have argued about which men disqualify a woman. רב חסדא points to a case with no argument at all. The next step shows how he proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
Everyone agrees
The widow of a man from a family whose lineage is in doubt (he might be a חלל)
Unfit to marry a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: עיסה literally means 'dough.' Here it describes a family where the lineage is mixed up and doubtful, like mixed dough. It has nothing to do with baking.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּאַלְמְנַת עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument between the תנאים to a point all of them agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אלמנת עיסה is unfit for כהונה according to every opinion.

steps.title: Proof from the most lenient opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows רב חסדא's point from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the most lenient of the תנאים, who says that if you can't marry the daughter, you can't marry the widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the most lenient of these תנאים? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He says: Anyone whose daughter you may marry, you may marry his widow; anyone whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the proof for רב חסדא. If even the most lenient opinion forbids her, then everyone does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disqualifies the fewest men, so he is the most lenient. The proof will rest on the second half of his rule, about the daughter you may not marry. The next step finishes the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is lenient
The תנאים, the teachers of the משנה period

phrases.english: Who is the most lenient of these tanna'im –
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and he says:
Anyone whose daughter you may marry –
you may marry his widow,
and anyone whose daughter you may not marry –
you may not marry his widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן מֵיקֵל בְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רב חסדא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That every תנא agrees an אלמנת עיסה is unfit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement, the most lenient opinion.

steps.title: The second half of his rule is about אלמנת עיסה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second half of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule comes to exclude, and answers: the אלמנת עיסה, who is unfit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does this come to exclude? It excludes a widow of questionable lineage, who is unfit for the priesthood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the words 'whose daughter you may not marry' are aimed at the case of אלמנת עיסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter from a family of doubtful lineage may not marry a כהן, since she might be a חללה. So by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own rule, the widow is also unfit. If even the most lenient תנא forbids her, everyone does, and רב חסדא is proven right.

keyTerms.meaning: What does this come to exclude?

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: an אלמנת עיסה is unfit for כהונה according to all opinions. The proof is that even the most lenient opinion, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, says 'whose daughter you may not marry, you may not marry his widow.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a firm practical ruling that holds no matter which תנא we follow in the larger argument.

phrases.english: To exclude what?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking what the second half of his rule ('whose daughter you may not marry') is coming to teach.

phrases.english: To exclude a widow of questionable lineage
that she is unfit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לְמַעוֹטֵי אַלְמְנַת עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 14 and confirms רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids an אלמנת עיסה to a כהן, so all the תנאים agree.

steps.title: The תנאים Who Disagree With רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב חסדא's 'all agree' leaves out רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who testified that an אלמנת עיסה is fit for כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא's statement leaves out these תנאים. We learned in a משנה: רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא testified that a widow from a family of doubtful lineage is fit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנאים whose opinion רב חסדא's statement does not include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said 'all agree' that an אלמנת עיסה is unfit. The גמרא now explains that 'all' means the three תנאים just discussed: the תנא קמא, רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. His statement is meant to rule against two other תנאים, who in a משנה in עדיות allow her to marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to leave out
Testified (gave testimony about a tradition they had received)
A widow from a family whose lineage is mixed or doubtful
Fit to marry a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב חסדא was simply wrong. His 'all agree' means the three תנאים just discussed, not every תנא anywhere. He is knowingly ruling against רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of these tannaim
as we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: עדיות 8:3

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira testified
about a widow from a family of doubtful lineage
that she is fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the limits of רב חסדא's 'all agree' by naming the תנאים who disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא hold that an אלמנת עיסה is fit for כהונה.

steps.title: Why the Widow Is Allowed: A Double Doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these תנאים are lenient, and answers that it is a ספק ספיקא, and a double doubt is ruled leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is a double doubt, and with a double doubt we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the lenient testimony and gives it right away: a double doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the אלמנת עיסה there are two separate layers of uncertainty about whether she is really flawed. When there are two doubts stacked like this, the rule is to be lenient. So these תנאים let her marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A double doubt; two separate uncertainties stacked together
Toward leniency

steps.whyThisMatters: ספק ספיקא is a basic tool all over הלכה. This is one of the places where it is used to allow something that would be forbidden with only one doubt.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is a double doubt,
and a double doubt is ruled leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the lenient view cited in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא allow the אלמנת עיסה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is a case of ספק ספיקא, and a double doubt is ruled leniently.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's 'all agree' covers the תנא קמא, רבי יוסי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagree and allow the אלמנת עיסה because of ספק ספיקא.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר: Definite With Definite Is Allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the words of the משנה where רבי אליעזר says that people with definite flaws may marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Definite ones with definite ones are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that follows about whose view is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says people whose flaw is certain (like a ממזר) may marry each other. But he forbids a certain flaw with a doubtful one (like a שתוקי or אסופי), and a doubtful one with another doubtful one. The rest of the section debates whether this is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those whose flaw is certain, marrying others whose flaw is certain
Permitted

phrases.english: Definite ones with definite ones are permitted.
phrases.notes: These are רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה. The doubtful cases are the שתוקי and the אסופי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַדָּאָן בְּוַדָּאָן מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by quoting רבי אליעזר's ruling from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, people with definite flaws may marry each other, but doubtful cases may not marry definite or doubtful ones.

steps.title: רב Rules Like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a ruling: we follow רבי אליעזר's rule about which flawed groups may marry each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling like רבי אליעזר means a doubtful case, like a שתוקי, may not marry a definite ממזרת. This ruling is what שמואל is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...
רב יהודה reporting a teaching of his teacher רב

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the משנה line just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר: doubtful cases may not marry definite ones.

steps.title: שמואל Objects Using הלל's Version
steps.stepSummary: שמואל challenges רב's ruling by quoting הלל's version, where all ten lineage groups may marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: When I said this in front of שמואל, he said to me: הלל teaches, 'Ten lineage groups came up from Babylonia, and all of them may marry one another.' And you say the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל attacks רב's ruling. He points to a version of the teaching that lets all the groups marry each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל's version says the flawed groups may all marry each other, even the doubtful ones like שתוקי and אסופי. That directly opposes רבי אליעזר, who forbids the doubtful ones. So שמואל holds that a doubtful case may marry a definite ממזרת, and he can't accept רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of...
הלל teaches (this is his version of the teaching)
Ten lineage groups
To marry one another

phrases.english: When I said it in front of Shmuel,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב יהודה, the one who reported רב's ruling.

phrases.english: he said to me: Hillel teaches:
ten lineage groups came up from Babylonia
and all of them are permitted to marry one another,
and you say the halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer?!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אֲמַר לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל's version lets all the groups marry each other, including the doubtful ones. That opposes רבי אליעזר, so how can the הלכה follow him?
steps.whatToRemember: רב rules like רבי אליעזר: a doubtful case may not marry a definite ממזר. שמואל follows הלל's version: everyone in these groups may marry each other.

steps.title: Setting Up a Contradiction: The Pregnant ארוסה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says both רב and שמואל seem to contradict themselves. It brings their dispute about a betrothed woman who became pregnant: רב says the child is a ממזר, and שמואל says the child is a שתוקי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now point out a contradiction between one statement of רב and another, and between one statement of שמואל and another. For it was said: a betrothed woman who became pregnant. רב said: the child is a ממזר. שמואל said: the child is a שתוקי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a contradiction. First it quotes the case it will use, and the next step spells out the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the case: a woman is only betrothed (an ארוסה) and becomes pregnant, and we don't know whose child it is. רב calls the child a ממזר. שמואל calls the child a שתוקי, a person whose father is unknown.

keyTerms.meaning: And point out a contradiction (set one statement against another)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין but before נישואין)
A child born from a forbidden relationship such as adultery
A person whose father is unknown, so his status is doubtful

phrases.english: And contrast a statement of Rav against another of Rav,
and a statement of Shmuel against another of Shmuel,
as it was stated:
a betrothed woman who became pregnant,
Rav said: the child is a mamzer.
And Shmuel said: the child is a shetuki.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִי דְּרַב אַדְּרַב וּרְמִי דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the positions of רב and שמואל from steps 19-20 and sets them against another dispute between them.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רב and שמואל with their views in steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their positions in the pregnant ארוסה case will be shown to clash with their positions on רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Spelling Out the Contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what each view means in practice. רב lets the child marry a ממזרת, and שמואל forbids it. Each is the opposite of what he said earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the child is a ממזר and may marry a ממזרת. שמואל said: the child is a שתוקי and may not marry a ממזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly why רב and שמואל each seem to contradict themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child's status is really a doubt. Yet רב lets him marry a definite ממזרת, even though רב follows רבי אליעזר, who forbids doubtful with definite. שמואל forbids him from marrying a ממזרת, even though he follows הלל, who allows all the groups to marry each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted to marry a female ממזר
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: The contradiction is not about the words 'ממזר' or 'שתוקי'. It is about the practical result: may a child of doubtful status marry a definite ממזרת?

phrases.english: Rav said: the child is a mamzer
and is permitted to marry a mamzeret,
and Shmuel said: the child is a shetuki
and is forbidden to marry a mamzeret.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר וּמוּתָּר בְּמַמְזֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction set up in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's and שמואל's rulings in the pregnant ארוסה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב permits a doubtful case with a definite ממזרת, against רבי אליעזר. שמואל forbids it, against הלל's version. Each one contradicts his own earlier view.

steps.title: Switch the Names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא solves the contradiction by reversing who said what in the pregnant ארוסה case: רב says the child is a שתוקי, and שמואל says the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רב says the child is a שתוקי, and שמואל says the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by swapping the two opinions in the ארוסה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, רב calls the child a שתוקי, who may not marry a ממזרת. That fits רבי אליעזר. שמואל calls the child a ממזר, who may marry a ממזרת. That fits הלל's version, where everyone in these groups may marry each other. Now both רב and שמואל are consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it; switch the names of who said what

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רב follows רבי אליעזר and calls the pregnant ארוסה's child a שתוקי. שמואל follows הלל's version and calls the child a ממזר.

phrases.english: Reverse it:
Rav said: the child is a shetuki,
and Shmuel said: the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 21-22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing which opinion belongs to which speaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב called the child a ממזר who may marry a ממזרת, and שמואל called the child a שתוקי who may not.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב calls the child a שתוקי, forbidden to a ממזרת, and שמואל calls the child a ממזר, permitted to a ממזרת. This matches each one's earlier view.

steps.title: Why do we need the dispute twice?
steps.stepSummary: After the switch, רב and שמואל disagree the same way in two different places, so the גמרא asks why both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that, after switching the opinions, רב and שמואל now hold the same positions in two different cases. It asks why we need both, and this question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב says שתוקי in the ארוסה case, his view matches his ruling like רבי אליעזר about the משנה's doubtful children. שמואל likewise matches his quote from הלל. So it looks like one disagreement is repeated, and the גמרא wants to know what each case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two? A standard question when the same idea seems to appear twice

phrases.english: Why do I need two?
phrases.notes: The two are רב and שמואל's argument about the משנה's doubtful children and their argument about the pregnant ארוסה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְתֵּי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from the switch in step 23, which made the two disagreements look like the same one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the two cases teaches that the other one does not.

steps.title: First reason both are needed: the unmarried woman's case alone
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the unmarried woman's case, we might think רב is lenient only there, because most men are permitted to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If it were said only in this case, I would think רב says it here because most men are fit with regard to her. But there, where most men are unfit with regard to her, I might say he agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why both cases are needed. It shows that the unmarried woman's case alone would not tell us רב's view about the ארוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unmarried woman is permitted to most men, so her child is probably not a ממזר, and רב calls the child only a doubt. A betrothed woman is forbidden to every man except her ארוס, so we might have thought רב agrees the child is a full ממזר. That is why the ארוסה case has to be taught too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed. Each case teaches something the other does not
Most men are permitted to her, so a child from them would not be a ממזר
Most men are forbidden to her
He agrees

phrases.english: It is needed, for if it were said only in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the משנה's case of an unmarried woman whose child is a שתוקי.

phrases.english: I would think it is in this case that רב says it,
because most men are fit with regard to her.
But there, where most men are unfit with regard to her,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the betrothed woman. Every man except her ארוס is forbidden to her.

phrases.english: I might say that he agrees with שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unmarried woman's case alone would not show that רב is also lenient for the ארוסה, where most men are forbidden to her.

steps.title: Second reason both are needed: the ארוסה's case alone
steps.stepSummary: If we only had the ארוסה case, we might think רב is lenient only there, because we can blame the pregnancy on her ארוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were said only in that case, I would think רב says it here because we can link the pregnancy to the ארוס. But in this other case, I might say he agrees with שמואל. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by looking at it the other way around. The ארוסה case alone would not tell us רב's view about the unmarried woman, so both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ארוסה case there is an easy, permitted explanation: the child is probably from her own ארוס. An unmarried woman has no such man to point to, so we might have thought רב agrees with שמואל there. Each case has its own reason to be lenient, so neither one teaches the other.

keyTerms.meaning: To link it to, meaning to blame the pregnancy on someone
The man she is betrothed to

steps.whatToRemember: Both cases are needed. The unmarried woman has 'most men are permitted to her' as a reason to be lenient, and the ארוסה has 'blame it on her ארוס'. Neither case teaches the other.

phrases.english: And if it were said only in that case,
phrases.notes: Now 'that case' is the pregnant ארוסה.

phrases.english: I would think it is in this case that רב says it,
because we can link the pregnancy to the ארוס,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected text and completes the word.

phrases.english: but in this other case I might say he agrees with שמואל,
phrases.notes: 'This other case' is the unmarried woman, who has no ארוס to blame the pregnancy on.

phrases.english: so both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 25 by looking at it from the other direction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ארוסה case alone would not show that רב is lenient for the unmarried woman, because only the ארוסה has her ארוס to blame the pregnancy on.

steps.title: Another answer: keep the opinions and explain רב's word ממזר
steps.stepSummary: Instead of switching the opinions, explain that רב's word ממזר only means the child may not marry a בת ישראל, not that he may marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, do not switch the opinions. What does רב mean by ממזר? Not that he may marry a ממזרת, but that he may not marry a בת ישראל. And שמואל said the child is a שתוקי, meaning he may not marry a בת ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to fix the contradiction from steps 21-22. This time it keeps רב saying ממזר and שמואל saying שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction came from reading רב's ממזר as 'he may marry a ממזרת', which goes against his ruling like רבי אליעזר. Now ממזר only means he may not marry a בת ישראל. That leaves room for him to be forbidden to a ממזרת as well, as a doubtful child. But שמואל's שתוקי now seems to mean the very same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, do not switch the opinions. Keep רב and שמואל as first quoted
A female ממזר
A Jewish woman with proper lineage

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'ממזר' is not a full statement of the child's status. It only tells us one rule: he may not marry a בת ישראל.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really, do not switch,
phrases.notes: Do not switch who said what, the way the גמרא did in the last answer.

phrases.english: and what does רב mean by ממזר?
Not that he is permitted to a ממזרת,
but that he is forbidden to a בת ישראל.
And שמואל said: the child is a שתוקי,
meaning he is forbidden to a בת ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם לָא תֵּיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the contradiction of steps 21-22, offered instead of the switch in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word (ממזר) instead of switching the opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's word ממזר meant the child may marry a ממזרת, which goes against his ruling like רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ממזר only means the child may not marry a בת ישראל, so it fits his ruling like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Then שמואל is saying the same as רב
steps.stepSummary: If שתוקי only means 'may not marry a בת ישראל', there is no disagreement between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. Under this reading, רב and שמואל would be saying exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both 'ממזר' and 'שתוקי' would mean only 'forbidden to a בת ישראל'. Then the two would not be arguing at all, so שמואל's word שתוקי must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as רב!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of שמואל's words in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that שמואל's שתוקי means forbidden to a בת ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that explanation רב and שמואל say the same thing, so their disagreement disappears.

steps.title: שתוקי means kept out of כהונה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's שתוקי means the child is 'silenced', meaning shut out, from the status of a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does שתוקי mean? That we silence him from the law of כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new meaning for שמואל's word שתוקי. It means the child is not treated as a כהן, even if the ארוס is one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שתוקי comes from 'silence'. Here it means we 'silence' the child's claim to be a כהן, so his ruling is about כהונה rather than marriage. This would give שמואל a statement separate from רב's.

keyTerms.meaning: We silence, meaning we shut him out of something
The status and rights of a כהן

phrases.english: Rather, what does שתוקי mean?
That we silence him from the law of כהונה.
phrases.notes: He means that even if the ארוס is a כהן, the child does not get the status of a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי שְׁתוּקִי – שֶׁמְּשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ מִדִּין כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 with a new meaning for שתוקי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a word a new meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתוקי means forbidden to a בת ישראל, which is the same as רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: שתוקי means the child is kept out of כהונה.

steps.title: That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the child is already shut out of a regular Jew's status, of course he is shut out of כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! Now that we silence him even from the law of a regular Jew, do we need to say it about the law of כהונה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the כהונה explanation. It would teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child may not even marry a בת ישראל, which is a lower level than כהונה. If he lacks the basic status, it goes without saying that he lacks the higher status of a כהן. שמואל would not need to say that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. A challenge that a statement teaches nothing new
Is it needed?

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא, הַשְׁתָּא מִדִּין יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשַׁתְּקִינַן לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: That is obvious! Now that we silence him from the law of a regular Jew,
do we need to say it about the law of כהונה?!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, הַשְׁתָּא מִדִּין יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשַׁתְּקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that שתוקי means kept out of כהונה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This follows automatically from a rule we already know, so שמואל would not need to say it.

steps.title: שתוקי means kept out of his father's property
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's שתוקי means the child does not inherit from the ארוס, who might be his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does שתוקי mean? That we silence him from his father's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third meaning for שתוקי. The child does not inherit from the man who might be his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now שתוקי is about inheritance, not marriage or כהונה. Since we cannot be sure the ארוס is the father, the child cannot claim a son's share of his property.

keyTerms.meaning: His father's property

phrases.english: Rather, what does שתוקי mean?
That we silence him from his father's property.
phrases.notes: 'His father' is the ארוס, the man who might be his father. The child does not inherit from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מַאי שְׁתוּקִי – שֶׁמְּשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ מִנִּכְסֵי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the כהונה explanation that step 30 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving a word a new meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתוקי means kept out of כהונה, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: שתוקי means the child does not inherit from the ארוס.

steps.title: That is obvious too: we don't know who his father is
steps.stepSummary: Of course he does not inherit, because nobody knows for sure who his father is.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! Do we know who his father is?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inheritance explanation as obvious as well. Someone whose father is unknown has nothing to inherit from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inheriting depends on proving who your father is. Since the child's father is in doubt, it seems obvious that he cannot take anyone's property, so שמואל's statement would again teach nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we know?
Who his father is

phrases.english: That is obvious! Do we know who his father is?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, מִי יָדְעִינַן אֲבוּהּ מַנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that שתוקי means the child does not inherit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a known father there is clearly no inheritance, so the statement adds nothing.

steps.title: The case is where the child seized the property
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's ruling is needed when the child already took hold of the ארוס's property. Even then, it is taken away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he seized the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל is talking about a child who already grabbed the ארוס's property. שמואל teaches that the property is still taken from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who is holding property has the advantage, and others must prove he has no right to it. שמואל teaches that here his grabbing does not help, and he must give it back. So שתוקי teaches something new, and it is different from רב's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a special case
He seized, meaning he took hold of the property

steps.whatToRemember: In the second answer the opinions stay as first quoted. רב's ממזר means only 'may not marry a בת ישראל'. שמואל's שתוקי means that even if the child grabbed the ארוס's property, it is taken away from him.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he seized it.
phrases.notes: The child took hold of the ארוס's property, saying the ארוס is his father, and שמואל says it is still taken from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דִּתְפַס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 32 by narrowing שמואל's ruling to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case where it teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inheritance ruling is obvious, since the father is unknown.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is needed where the child already seized the property. Even so, it is taken away from him.

steps.title: שתוקי means 'checked': the mother is asked and believed
steps.stepSummary: A new reading of שמואל's word: שתוקי really means בדוקי. We ask the mother, and if she says the father was a fit man, she is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say this: what does שתוקי mean? It means 'checked.' We check with his mother, and if she says, 'I was with a fit man,' she is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more explanation of what שמואל meant by calling the child שתוקי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers read שתוקי as something bad for the child: shut out of כהונה, or unable to inherit. This answer reads it in a good direction. The child's status is 'checked' by asking the mother, and her claim that the father was fit is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
'Checked': someone whose status is determined by asking
'I was with a fit man': the mother's claim about the father
She is believed

steps.confusionAlert: Here שתוקי is NOT about silencing the child. It is a different reading that turns the word into 'checked,' which helps the child.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
What is 'שתוקי'? It means 'checked,'
meaning that they check with his mother,
and if she says, 'I was with a fit man,' she is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: מַאי שְׁתוּקִי – בְּדוּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a completely different reading of שתוקי instead of the 'silenced' readings in steps 29-33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שתוקי means the child is pushed away from some status or right.
steps.terutzMaskana: שתוקי means בדוקי: the mother is asked, and her claim that the father was fit is believed.

steps.title: Didn't שמואל already rule like רבן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this new reading follows רבן גמליאל. But שמואל already ruled like רבן גמליאל in a different case, so why would he say it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? רבן גמליאל's? But שמואל already said that once! As we learned in a משנה: if a woman was pregnant, and people asked her, 'What is the status of this fetus?' and she said, 'It is from so-and-so, and he is a כהן,' then רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say she is believed, and רבי יהושע says she is not believed. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading: if שמואל means the mother is believed, he would be repeating a ruling he already gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Believing the mother about who the father was is exactly רבן גמליאל's view in the משנה in כתובות. שמואל already ruled like רבן גמליאל there. So reading שתוקי as בדוקי seems to make שמואל's statement here unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whose opinion?
One time, meaning 'he already said it'
Pregnant
What is its nature or status?
The תנא who believes the woman about who the father is

phrases.english: Whose view is this? רבן גמליאל's?
But שמואל already said that once!
As we learned: if she was pregnant,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in כתובות 13a. It is talking about an unmarried woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ: מָה טִיבוֹ שֶׁל עוּבָּר זֶה?
phrases.english: and people said to her: 'What is the status of this fetus?'
and she answered, 'It is from so-and-so, and he is a כהן,'

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: רבן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר say: she is believed.
רבי יהושע says: she is not believed.
And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן – כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל? הָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the בדוקי reading by pointing out that it would make שמואל repeat himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of שתוקי as בדוקי (step 34)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל already ruled like רבן גמליאל, who believes the mother. So a second statement with the same message would be pointless.

steps.title: Both rulings are needed: most men are fit for a single woman, but unfit for a betrothed one
steps.stepSummary: Both rulings are needed. With a single woman, most men are fit for her. With a betrothed woman, most men are forbidden to her, so we might not have believed her without this second ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If we only had the ruling from there, I would have said: there, most men are fit with regard to her. But here, where most men are unfit with regard to her, say she is not believed. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל had to say his ruling twice, because the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unmarried woman is permitted to most men, so her claim that the father was fit already matches what usually happens. A betrothed woman is forbidden to everyone except her ארוס, so the odds are against her claim. Without this second ruling, we might have thought she is not believed in that harder case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: both statements are needed
I would have thought
Most men are fit (permitted to her)
Most men are unfit (forbidden to her)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling about the betrothed woman teaches something new: the mother is believed even when most men are forbidden to her.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if we only had it from there, I would have said:
there, most men are fit with regard to her,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the unmarried woman in the משנה. Most men are permitted to her.

phrases.english: but here, where most men are unfit with regard to her,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the betrothed woman. Everyone except her ארוס is forbidden to her.

phrases.english: you might say she is not believed. So it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי מֵהָתָם הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 35 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing both statements are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the משנה alone, one might believe the mother only where most men are fit for her.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's second ruling teaches that she is believed even where most men are forbidden to her.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a כותי may not marry a כותית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אלעזר's ruling that one כותי may not marry another כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: and similarly, רבי אלעזר says: a כותי may not marry a כותית.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a ruling of רבי אלעזר about כותים marrying each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because people of the same group usually may marry each other. The גמרא will now ask for the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A Samaritan, a member of a group whose Jewish status was in doubt
A Samaritan woman

phrases.english: It was taught: and similarly, רבי אלעזר says:
A כותי may not marry a כותית.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: וְכֵן רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the שתוקי discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, a כותי may not marry a כותית.

steps.title: What is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר forbids a כותי from marrying a כותית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי אלעזר's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people from the same group would normally be a fine match. So the גמרא wants to know what makes a כותי forbidden to a כותית.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 37.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a כותי may not marry a כותית.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a כותי is treated like a convert's descendant after ten generations
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that חכמים treated a כותי like a convert's descendant after ten generations. Such a person may no longer marry a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: they treated him like a convert after ten generations. As it was taught: a convert, up to ten generations, may marry a ממזרת. From then on, he may not marry a ממזרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the reason for רבי אלעזר's ruling and supports it with a ברייתא about converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert's family may marry a ממזרת for ten generations. After that, people no longer remember their roots, so they are treated like ordinary Jews and may not. A כותי is treated like that later stage. So he may not marry someone of flawed lineage, and that includes another כותי.

keyTerms.meaning: They made him, meaning חכמים treated him as
A convert
Ten generations
A woman born from a forbidden union
From here on

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
They treated him like a convert after ten generations,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כותי. 'They' are the חכמים.

phrases.english: as it was taught: a convert, up to ten generations,
is permitted to marry a ממזרת;
from then on, he is forbidden to marry a ממזרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: עֲשָׂאוּהוּ כְּגֵר לְאַחַר עֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כותי is treated like a convert's descendant after ten generations, who may not marry someone of flawed lineage.

steps.title: Some say: until the memory of idol worship is forgotten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a second opinion. A convert's family may marry a ממזרת until people forget their idol-worshipping roots, no matter how many generations pass.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: until the name of idol worship is forgotten from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that רב יוסף quoted finishes with a different opinion about when a convert's family loses permission to marry a ממזרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets a fixed limit of ten generations. The 'some say' opinion instead depends on memory: as long as people still remember the family came from idol worshippers, they may still marry a ממזרת.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: introduces a second opinion
That it is forgotten (literally, 'sinks away')
Idol worship

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מִמֶּנּוּ.
phrases.english: until the name of idol worship is forgotten from him.
phrases.notes: He means: the permission to marry a ממזרת lasts until people forget that this family came from idol worshippers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 39 with a second opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A convert's family may marry a ממזרת until people forget their idol-worshipping roots.

steps.title: אביי shows the convert comparison does not fit
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's comparison. A long-ago convert who marries a known ממזרת looks like a regular Jew marrying a ממזרת. Two כותים are the same as each other, so no one would get the wrong idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are the cases really alike? There, the man comes from a convert family from long ago, and the woman is a known ממזרת. People will say: a regular Jew is marrying a ממזרת! Here, the man and the woman are both the same kind of person.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer from Step 39. He shows that the reason we stop a long-ago convert from marrying a ממזרת does not apply to two כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The convert rule is about how things look. People see an 'old' convert family as ordinary Jews, so his marriage to a known ממזרת looks like a regular Jew marrying a ממזרת. Two כותים share the same status. If we treat the man as a full Jew, we must treat the woman the same way, so nothing looks wrong. That means רב יוסף's reason cannot explain רבי אלעזר's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they really alike? A common way to reject a comparison.
An 'old' convert, meaning the family converted long ago and people see them as ordinary Jews
A 'new' ממזרת, meaning her status is known and fresh in people's minds
This one and that one, meaning both sides
Like each other, the same

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not say converts may marry ממזרות forever. He only says the reason for stopping the old convert (people would think a regular Jew is marrying a ממזרת) does not fit the case of two כותים.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Is it comparable?
There, he is an old convert and she is a new ממזרת,
so people say: It is a Jewish man
who is marrying a ממזרת.
Here, this one and that one
are the same as each other.
phrases.notes: Both the man and the woman are כותים, so they have the same status.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's explanation in Step 39 by showing the comparison to a convert does not hold.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a כותי and a convert family after ten generations.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The convert rule exists because people would mistake him for a regular Jew marrying a known ממזרת. Two כותים have the same status, so no such mistake can happen.

steps.title: רב דימי gives a new reason: רבי אלעזר follows רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting רב יוסף's answer, the גמרא brings a new explanation in the name of רב דימי: רבי אלעזר holds like רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: רבי אלעזר holds like רבי ישמעאל,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the old answer and starts a new one. It is setting up the next move: the following lines will explain what רבי ישמעאל held and why it leads to רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא tells us the previous explanation has been dropped. The new idea is that רבי אלעזר's ruling against a כותי marrying a כותית is not his own new reasoning. It comes from an earlier opinion of רבי ישמעאל, which the גמרא is about to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Shows the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming.
When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings from there
He holds like, meaning he agrees with that person's view
